newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end down ahead of housing starts report.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end down ahead of housing starts report.

text.p: CME lumber futures retreated after posting a new contract high in May early as evening-up ahead of Wednesday's March U.S. housing starts report weighed on the market, traders said.
May set a new contract high of $417.50 per tbf before prices retreated to close $4.70 per tbf lower to $0.40 higher. May paced the setback at $409.40 and July ended at $0.20 lower at $396.50 per tbf.
Initial strength reflected the recent strong tone to the cash market. But cash trading slowed and the housing report was expected to show a slowdown in building, they said.
Economists on average estimated the housing starts report would show an annualized 1.46 million units in March, down from 1.528 million units in February.
